title: How Cannabis Prohibition Hobbles The Fight Against Cocaine “Flooding” Into Europe, And Against Russian State Sponsored Terrorism and Hurts the Economy of Morocco

content_html_sanitized:
First, the good news: the center right coalition that is going to form the next German government has announced that it is not going to make any changes in the new law legalizing recreational use, and Cannabis Social Clubs, as well as easing medical access. 

However, they will be “reviewed” sometime in the Autumn. See CANNABIS LEGALISATION: WHAT PLANS DOES  GERMANY’S INCOMING GOVERNMENT HAVE?


Meanwhile, Deutsche Welle (German Wave) Germany’s state owned news service has an excellent article with a long video, “Why is cocaine flooding Germany?” (in English) about the international trade in cocaine from Latin America to Europe, especially through the shipping container ports of Rotterdam, Antwerp, and Germany’s own Hamburg.


Of course, cocaine is “off topic” for MarijuanaNews, but marijuana prohibition created the infrastructure for cocaine smuggling through Mexico and for distribution in the U.S., and to a lesser degree still does in both the U.S. and Europe. 


In fact, Morocco is another country that has also been a victim of cannabis prohibition by creating the infrastructure for cocaine smuggling. See Moroccan Authorities Seize Over 136 Kilograms of Cocaine at El Guerguerat Border 

It would be in everyone’s best interest to let Morocco develop its hashish culture and supply Europe legally with safe cannabis concentrates, as well as being a part of its growing tourism sector. 

From  Legal cannabis offers Morocco a route into Europe By Alice Morrison September 20, 2024 (Excellent website) “The King of Morocco, Mohammed Vl, has taken the unprecedented step of pardoning more than 4,800 illegal cannabis farmers in the north of his country.  Mohammed El Guerrouj, the head of the National Agency for the Regulation of Cannabis-Related Activities (Anrac), said the decision was made to encourage farmers to grow cannabis legally and to improve living conditions. Anrac also reported that it had approved nearly 3,000 licences for cannabis cultivation and production so far this year, mainly in the provinces of Taounate, Chefchaouen and Al Hoceïma, up from 609 issued in the whole of 2023. The moves are part of Morocco’s strategy to legitimise a once-buoyant criminal enterprise, which it believes could be worth billions of dollars in legal trade.

Tom Blickman, a policy researcher and expert in the drugs industry at the Transnational Institute, a think-tank based in Amsterdam, told AGBI the initiatives show that the policies around cannabis were relaxing in Morocco. The easing started in 2021 with the passing of a law that allowed cannabis growing for medical and industrial purposes.”

But there are two impediments to that, Spain and France, which has one of the highest rates of cannabis use in Europe. 

Both refuse even to consider legalizing cannabis, despite the fact that the tragic 2004 bombing of Madrid's Atocha train station which killed 193 people and injured over 2,000, was financed by smuggling hashish from Morocco. Plus France has longstanding cultural ties with North Africa, which are damaged by cannabis prohibition.

Of course, Hashish  has been a part of North African culture far longer than marijuana has been for Mexico, but black markets are the same everywhere. They let you pick your poison. See 42 arrested in Spain for trafficking cannabis and heroin  

One thing that cannabis prohibition still does everywhere is drain finite law enforcement resources from genuine problems, including violent organized crime and Islamic terrorism and Russian state sponsored terrorism. See Russia is conducting ‘state-sponsored terrorism’ against Europe, EU chief diplomat warns 

All governments have finite resources and consequently must have priorities. In this context, how can any government justify saying cannabis is a greater threat than organized crime and terrorism? See France Making An Even Bigger Mess of Its Cannabis Policy, But Finally About to Legalize Medical After Only Thirty Years.
